notes: Warren Buffett Biography Flash a weekly Biography. In the past few days, Warren Buffett’s most consequential story has been his formal retreat from Berkshire Hathaway. According to Berkshire’s September 18 company announcement, Buffett is now chairman emeritus and remains a director, while his son Howard Buffett has become non executive chairman and Greg Abel continues as chief executive. The change ends more than six decades of Warren Buffett serving as Berkshire’s chairman, making it one of the defining final chapters of his business biography. Buffett himself has made no widely reported public appearance in the past few days, and there are no verified new social media posts from him that materially change the story. Much of the online conversation has instead focused on his farewell message to shareholders, particularly the phrase Father Time always wins. Reports describing a new personal retirement announcement should be treated cautiously unless confirmed by Berkshire or Buffett directly. The business activity carrying Buffett’s name is now being executed under Abel’s leadership, but it reflects the long term style Buffett built. CNBC reports that Berkshire bought about 53.6 million dollars more of Lennar shares across three trading days, lifting its stake to roughly 11.2 percent, or about 2.1 billion dollars. The buying pace slowed, but the move signals continued confidence in housing as a long range investment. Berkshire also completed its 6.8 billion dollar purchase of homebuilder Taylor Morrison this summer, according to company reporting summarized by AOL. Combined with Clayton Properties Group, the deal makes Berkshire one of America’s largest homebuilding forces. Berkshire has also reportedly repurchased about 4.5 billion dollars of its own shares in the second quarter, while maintaining an enormous cash and Treasury position. For a lighter headline, Forbes data reported by CNBC and VnExpress placed Buffett back among the world’s ten richest people, with an estimated fortune around 142 to 143 billion dollars, ahead of Zara founder Amancio Ortega. That ranking is market driven and can change quickly. Analysts and commentators are speculating about whether Berkshire can match Buffett’s performance, but those judgments are opinion, not established fact. Buffett remains a director and chairman emeritus, not the company’s operating leader. Thank you for listening.
